stances_toward.note: NATO co-member with a bilateral military cooperation agreement since 1992 (Turkey backed Albania's NATO entry; its 800-strong brigade took part in Operation Alba, 1997). Erdogan opened the Diyanet-funded Namazgah mosque in Tirana on 10 Oct 2024, signed a joint declaration on a strategic partnership and promised drones, equipment and training; Rama called the drones a deterrent. Not a plain ally in outlook: Rama contradicted Erdogan on Gaza at the same visit, and Turkey is one of several suppliers, not the sole one. Bond - affinity: Ottoman heritage and a Muslim-majority population (Gallup: 73% of Albanians call Turkey friendly); no kinship.

stances_toward.note: No diplomatic relations and a closed land border since 1993; Ankara is the treaty ally of Azerbaijan, which Yerevan graded a mortal enemy until 2023. Normalisation is real but partial: Erdogan congratulated Pashinyan after the June 2026 election (first time), the Margara checkpoint opened only for humanitarian cargo on 12-22 Jun 2026, the Akhalkalaki-Kars rail link through Georgia opened for Armenian trade on 24 May 2026 and a working group met in Kars on 28 Apr 2026 on the Gyumri-Kars line. Not 'partner' because no relations exist and the genocide question is unresolved; the grade is 'rival' warming. Bond - grievance: the 1915 genocide and Turkey's denial.

stances_toward.note: Treaty alliance: the 2010 Agreement on Strategic Partnership and Mutual Assistance and the Shusha Declaration on Allied Relations (15 Jun 2021), under which the two coordinate their armed forces if a third state threatens either's independence or territorial integrity. Kin (Turkic, 'one nation, two states'). Joint exercises (Unwavering Brotherhood, 26 Mar-1 Apr 2026), defence-industry talks at ADEX (30 Sep 2026), Erdogan's call after the Nakhchivan strike. The one visible friction is Ankara's normalisation with Armenia (direct trade preparations completed on 11 May 2026), which Turkey has tied to a peace deal acceptable to Baku, so it does not cut against the alliance.

stances_toward.note: Turkey is the Bosniak-led side's patron: Becirovic was received by Erdogan in Istanbul on 14 Mar 2025 during the Dodik crisis, thanked him for Turkey's support for Bosnia's Euro-Atlantic path, and met the Turkish ambassador again in Feb 2026. Partner, not ally: no treaty guarantee, and Ankara keeps good relations with Belgrade (and with Banja Luka), so its weight is political, not protective. Bond affinity: Ottoman heritage and the Muslim Bosniak community; the Croat and Serb thirds do not share it.

No political conditions and no interest in Georgian Dream's domestic course. Bond none: interest only.

stances_toward.note: NATO co-member (the dataset would derive 'ally') with a layered bilateral track that the Commission calls 'intensified': a framework agreement on military cooperation (Oct 2024), Turkish donations of military equipment to the army, a political declaration in Istanbul (28 Feb 2025) setting up a High-Level Cooperation Council and updating the free trade agreement, and a second Erdogan-Mickoski meeting at Dolmabahce on 13 Jun 2026. Turkish investment approaches USD 2bn and bilateral trade nearly USD 1bn (Erdogan, Feb 2025). Partner and not ally because there is no bilateral guarantee beyond the common NATO seat. Bond - affinity: Ottoman heritage, Muslim minority, and a patron outside the EU.

Turkey was the second-largest source of FDI in January-October 2025 (EUR 110.9m) and 4.3% of foreign overnights. Warming because the Council and the investment build-up are new. Bond - affinity: the Bosniak and Albanian Muslim communities and Ottoman heritage, not kinship.

stances_toward.note: Vučić calls Turkey 'an important partner for Serbia'; joint declaration (Feb 2026) on foreign policy, trade, defence industry, energy; USD 5bn trade target. Structural check: Turkey recognises Kosovo, has a free-trade agreement with it (in force 2019), sells it Bayraktar drones and supports the KSF (see XKX); Belgrade accepts that because Ankara asks Pristina to de-escalate and trades with both, so the grade is transactional, with no bond.

stances_toward.note: Black Sea gatekeeper that sells Ukraine drones and keeps its ties with Moscow: Ankara hosted the NATO summit (7-8 Jul 2026) with Zelensky invited, backs Ukrainian sovereignty over Crimea, offered to host trilateral talks (Zelensky 'very open', Sep 2026) and to monitor a Black Sea ceasefire. Bilateral trade is only about USD 1bn, with a target of USD 10bn after the Zelensky-Erdogan meeting in New York. The free-trade agreement was signed on 3 Feb 2022. Partner, not ally: no treaty of alliance, and Ankara balances between Kyiv and Moscow. Bond - none.

stances_toward.note: Free-trade agreement in force since 2019, bilateral trade of about USD 750m-1bn, TB2 drones and a military-financial cooperation agreement, Erdogan-Kurti meeting at the UN on 21 Sep 2026. Bond - affinity: Ottoman heritage and a shared Muslim community; no kinship.
